title: I asked Claude "make something cool with LittleJS" overnight and woke up to up to 40,000 starlings. 🐦
author: Slackluster
selftext:
I gave Claude one prompt, "make something cool with LittleJS to show it off," and let it work overnight on its own!

LittleJS is my tiny, fast, open source JavaScript game engine: [https://github.com/KilledByAPixel/LittleJS](https://github.com/KilledByAPixel/LittleJS)

LittleJS AI, a plugin that teaches AI assistants to make games with LittleJS: [https://github.com/KilledByAPixel/LittleJS-AI](https://github.com/KilledByAPixel/LittleJS-AI)

comments.author: PulIthEld
comments.body: ECS pattern?  I also have a js game engine.

replies.author: Slackluster
replies.body:
Nope, not ECS. LittleJS is plain object-oriented. Everything in the world is an `EngineObject`: you extend it, override `update()` and `render()`, and the engine keeps the list and handles physics, collision, drawing and parent/child attachment for you.

For small and medium games I find that much quicker to write and easier to read than splitting things into components and systems. Nothing stops you from adding your own component layer on top if a game needs it, though!
